resources.string: PAudio is not a medical device. These results are estimates for music listening only and are not a medical diagnosis. Phones and earphones can\'t be calibrated like clinical equipment, so hearing loss that is equal across all frequencies can\'t be detected. If you notice changes in your hearing, ringing, or pain, see a doctor or audiologist.
Take a hearing test with your headphones to see an estimated audiogram and summary here.
Values are estimated relative to your better ear at 1 and 2 kHz. They are not calibrated clinical measurements.
Points marked with a down arrow are beyond test range: you did not hear them at the loudest level PAudio allows, so the real value may be higher. That does not mean no hearing at those frequencies.
Shown as a number only. There is no grade for these very high pitches, and they naturally fade with age and noise exposure.
Some of these points are beyond the test range, so the real value may be higher.

This grade is approximate. It uses the WHO 2021 bands on your better ear without the 0.5 kHz test, and it cannot detect hearing loss that is flat across all frequencies or limited to low frequencies. It is not a statement that your hearing is healthy or unhealthy.
Your ears may differ by 15 dB or more across neighbouring frequencies. This can have many ordinary causes, such as earwax or headphone fit. If it persists, consider seeing an audiologist.
You pressed the button during some silent moments, so this test may be less reliable. Consider repeating it in a quiet place.

resources.string: Only tests with the same profile and the same headphones are compared, because different headphones sound different.
Take another test with the same headphones to see a trend.
Pitch runs from left to right, from 1 kHz to 14 kHz. Estimated level runs from top to bottom: points closer to the top mean you heard softer sounds, points lower down mean sounds had to be louder.

A red circle is your right ear and a blue cross is your left ear. A down arrow marks a point beyond test range: you did not hear it at the loudest level PAudio allows, so the real value may be higher. A dashed outline marks a point that was inconsistent between repeats.
The bands follow the WHO 2021 hearing grades. The grade shown is approximate: it comes from your better ear, uses 1, 2 and 4 kHz, and is estimated from phone and earphone playback.

Phones and earphones cannot be calibrated like clinical equipment, so PAudio compares your ears and pitches with each other. Hearing loss that is the same at every pitch, or limited to low pitches, cannot be detected this way. A result in the normal range does not mean your hearing is fine.

The trend only compares tests taken with the same profile and the same headphones. A change may come from the headphones, their fit or the room, so consider repeating a test before drawing conclusions.
